title: Password: Recover NSID and Reset Password

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Go to the NSID password recovery page and click "I forgot my password".
2. Enter your NSID and click "Continue".
3. Choose email, SMS, or security questions to verify your identity.
4. Enter the verification code or answers and submit them.
5. Enter and confirm a new password that meets the password requirements, then click "Reset Password".
6. Wait at least 15 minutes for the new password to synchronize with USask services.
7. Update the saved password on applicable VPN, Wi-Fi, Apple device, mail, and password-manager accounts.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text:
After a password change you must update saved wireless networks, VPN, phone mail apps and any password manager.

Synchronisation can take several minutes; a failure immediately afterwards is usually a saved old password.

title: Wireless: Connect to uofs-secure Network

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Select uofs-secure from the available Wi-Fi networks.
3. Enter your NSID in the format the device requires and your PAWS password.
4. Accept the server certificate for iseberg.usask.ca.
5. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On Windows
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Select the Wi-Fi icon from the bottom right task bar.
3. Select uofs-secure and click Connect.
4. Enter your NSID as the username and your PAWS password, then select OK.
5. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On macOS
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Select the Wi-Fi icon from the top right menu and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter your NSID as the username and your PAWS password, then select Join.
4. Select Show Certificate, check Always trust iseberg.usask.ca and select Continue.
5. Enter your Mac administrator username and password at the Certificate Trust Settings prompt, then select Update Settings.
6. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On iPhone or iPad
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Open Settings, select Wi-Fi and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter your NSID as the username and your PAWS password, then select Join.
4. Verify the server is named iseberg.usask.ca and select Trust.
5. Check that a checkmark appears beside uofs-secure and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Open Settings, select Network & Internet (or Connections), select Wi-Fi and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter the following settings:
   — EAP method: PEAP
   — Phase 2 authentication: MSCHAPV2
   — CA certificate: Use System Certificates
   — Online certificate status: Request status
   — Identity: your NSID
   — Password: your PAWS password
   — Domain: usask.ca
4. Select Connect.
5. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On ChromeOS
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Open Settings, select Network > Wi-Fi and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter the following settings:
   — EAP Method: PEAP
   — EAP Phase 2 authentication: MSCHAPv2
   — Server CA certificate: Default
   — Subject match: iseberg.usask.ca
   — Domain suffix match: usask.ca
   — Identity: your NSID in the format abc123@usask.ca
   — Password: your PAWS password
4. Select Connect.
5. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On Linux
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Open Settings, select Network, select Wireless and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter the following settings in the authentication window:
   — Wi-Fi Security: WPA & WPA2 Enterprise
   — Authentication: Protected EAP (PEAP)
   — CA Certificate: DigiCert Global Root G2
   — PEAP Version: Automatic
   — Inner authentication: MSCHAPv2
   — Username: your NSID in the format abc123@usask.ca
   — Password: your PAWS password
4. Select Connect.
5. Check that the connection works and verify internet access.

sections.heading: On reMarkable
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and PAWS password is current.
   — If you recently reset your password, remove the saved uofs-secure network and join it again.
   — If the CA certificate can't be set to Use System Certificates, install the DigiCert certificate first.
2. Open the hamburger menu, select Settings, select Wi-Fi and select uofs-secure.
3. Enter the following settings:
   — EAP Method: PEAP
   — Phase 2 authentication: MSCHAPv2
   — Identity: your NSID
   — Password: your PAWS password
4. Select Connect.
5. Check that the connection works.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Username format: NSID only on Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and reMarkable; full NSID@usask.ca on ChromeOS and Linux.

title: Multi Factor Authentication: Set Up and Troubleshoot

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Sign in to the Authenticator app and link it with PAWS.
2. Check everything on myprofile.usask.ca.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text:
A prompt asking to check a registered device is waiting for an approval tap, not a typed code.

When number matching is on, the number shown on screen is typed into the app.

Part of this is done by the service desk. If the steps above don't resolve it, open a ticket with the service desk.

title: Microsoft 365: Install on a Personal Device

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Sign in to office.com with your USask ID.
2. Select Install apps and download the Microsoft 365 installer.
3. Run the installer and wait for the installation to finish.
4. Open an Office app and sign in with your USask ID to activate it.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: If the browser version works but the desktop apps fail, the cause is usually device registration rather than your licence.

title: Printing: Denied or Delayed Print Jobs

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Check the available print credit on the account.
2. Check the job in the print queue for a denial reason.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: A denied job is most often an insufficient balance rather than a printer fault.

title: Software: Install from the Managed Software Catalogue

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open the software catalogue on the managed device.
2. Locate the application and choose install.
3. Wait for the installation to complete and open the application.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text:
The catalogue is only available on university managed Windows devices.

Off campus the device must be on the VPN for the catalogue to populate.

title: O365 Email: Set up USask email in Outlook on Windows

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open Outlook and enter your USask email address.
2. Sign in with your USask credentials on the Microsoft sign-in page.
3. Approve the MFA prompt on your phone.
4. Finish the account setup and confirm the mailbox loaded.

title: Apple Mail: Setup on iPhone or iPad

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open Settings > Mail > Accounts > Add Account and choose Microsoft Exchange.
2. Enter your USask email address and select Sign In.
3. Sign in with your USask credentials and approve the MFA prompt.
4. Accept the permissions and choose Mail, Contacts and Calendars to sync.
5. Save the account and confirm the mailbox loaded in the Mail app.

title: O365 Email: Android Phone - Set up the Gmail App

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open the Gmail app and select Add another account.
2. Choose Exchange and Office 365 and enter your USask email address.
3. Sign in with your USask credentials and approve the MFA prompt.
4. Accept the permissions and finish the account setup.
5. Confirm the mailbox loaded in the Gmail app.

title: Access and Use the USask Remote Computer Lab

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open PAWS and log in.
2. Search for Remote Lab and click Software and Computer Labs.
3. Click Remote Computer Lab.
4. Click Common Desktop.
5. Click Connect in Session Settings.
6. Log in with your NSID and PAWS password.

title: Virtual Private Network (VPN)

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Confirm your NSID is active and password is current.
2. Use the VPN only when you are off campus, not while connected to the campus network.
3. Install and configure the USask VPN client software for your device.
4. Connect to the USask VPN service at vpn.usask.ca using your NSID and password.
5. Confirm the VPN connected successfully and you can access USask resources.

title: Zoom at USask - Activate Your Account

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. USask members need to opt in to Zoom before first use.
2. Sign in to My Profile.
3. Go to the Opt In Services section and click Edit.
4. Enable Zoom and click Save Changes.
5. Wait about 30 minutes after opting in before using Zoom. Signing in sooner may show the error "something went wrong while you tried signing in with SSO".
6. Sign in at https://usask-ca.zoom.us or through the Web Conferencing channel in PAWS, not at zoom.us, which returns an error with USask credentials.

title: SharePoint Online at USask

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Check whether what you need is part of USask's SharePoint Online service.
2. Some features belonged to USask's former on-premise SharePoint server and are not part of SharePoint Online.
3. For learning SharePoint itself, see Microsoft's SharePoint introduction.

sections.heading: Depending on your situation
sections.text:
Custom permissions are not supported; each site has only two groups, Owners and Members.

ICT does not build or maintain custom workflows or forms.

ICT does not help format or customize sites.

Email-enabled lists and libraries are not available in SharePoint Online.

Nintex Forms and Nintex Workflows are not available in SharePoint Online.

title: Microsoft Teams at USask

sections.text:
1. Check that you are eligible for a USask Teams account.
2. Install Microsoft Teams on your personal device from the Microsoft Teams website.
3. Open Microsoft Teams on your device.
4. Sign in with your Office 365 username in the format nsid@usask.ca and your password.
5. Confirm you are signed in and can access Teams.

sections.heading: On Windows
sections.text:

2. Install Microsoft Teams on your work device via Software Center for Windows.
3. Open Microsoft Teams on your device.
4. Sign in with your Office 365 username in the format nsid@usask.ca and your password.
5. Confirm you are signed in and can access Teams.

sections.heading: On macOS
sections.text:
1. Check that you are eligible for a USask Teams account.
2. Install Microsoft Teams on your work device via Self Service for Mac.
3. Open Microsoft Teams on your device.
4. Sign in with your Office 365 username in the format nsid@usask.ca and your password.
5. Confirm you are signed in and can access Teams.

sections.heading: On iPhone or iPad
sections.text:
1. Check that you are eligible for a USask Teams account.
2. Install Microsoft Teams on your mobile device from the App Store.
3. Open Microsoft Teams on your device.
4. Sign in with your Office 365 username in the format nsid@usask.ca and your password.
5. Confirm you are signed in and can access Teams.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
1. Check that you are eligible for a USask Teams account.
2. Install Microsoft Teams on your mobile device from Google Play.
3. Open Microsoft Teams on your device.
4. Sign in with your Office 365 username in the format nsid@usask.ca and your password.
5. Confirm you are signed in and can access Teams.

title: OneDrive: Saving files to USask OneDrive

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Go to login.microsoftonline.com and sign in with your NSID@usask.ca and NSID password.
2. Open OneDrive to your University of Saskatchewan OneDrive folder.
3. Click Upload, select Files, choose the files you wanted to upload and click Open.
4. Confirm the files uploaded successfully to your OneDrive.
5. You can also save straight from Word, Excel or PowerPoint: select File > Save As > OneDrive - University of Saskatchewan.

title: JADE: Map a drive to a departmental JADE share

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Find out the name of your department's JADE share.
   — Map a network drive on your computer to the share on \\jade.
   — If your department uses a Domain DFS root, map the drive to it under \\usask.ca instead.
2. Confirm you can open the share and access your files.

title: JADE: Can't access a share

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Make sure you are signed in to your computer with the account that should have access to the share.
2. Make sure your computer is connected to the campus network, wired or wireless.
3. Check whether you can see the share by browsing to \\jade.
4. Try other JADE shares under \\jade2, \\jade3 and \\jade4. If they open, the servers are up.
   — If you are not a member of the share's permission groups, ask the person who manages the share to request access for you.
   — If you were only recently added to the share's group, the change may not have taken effect yet.
   — Log off and back on to your computer so new group membership takes effect.
5. Confirm you can access the share.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Part of this is done by the service desk. If the steps above don't resolve it, open a ticket with the service desk.

title: SPSS: Getting Started

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Open PAWS and log in.
2. Search for Remote Lab and click Software and Computer Labs.
3. Click Remote Computer Lab.
4. Click Common Desktop.
5. Click Connect in Session Settings.
6. Log in with your NSID and PAWS password.
7. Open SPSS from the Remote Computer Lab desktop.
8. Confirm SPSS opened in the remote session.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Students access SPSS through the Remote Computer Lab rather than installing it on a personal device.

title: ArcGIS Pro: How to Install

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Confirm your ArcGIS Online account is active using your USask NSID and password.
2. Sign in to your ArcGIS Online organization account, click your username and select My settings.
3. Open the Licenses tab and confirm ArcGIS Pro is listed with the Download ArcGIS Pro link.
4. Click Download ArcGIS Pro, review the language setting and click Download.
5. Install the Microsoft .NET framework as the required prerequisite.
6. Run the ArcGIS Pro installer and install with the "Anyone who uses this machine (all users)" option to enable license management.
7. Review and agree to the Educational program license terms.
8. Launch ArcGIS Pro and select Your ArcGIS organization's URL.
9. Enter "spatialsk", click Continue and select University of Saskatchewan.
10. Sign in with your NSID and password to authorize the license.
11. Confirm ArcGIS Pro opened with a valid license.

title: Class Registration: Request a class override

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Attempt registration under Register for Classes, add the class by CRN to the summary and click Submit.
2. Review the error by hovering over "Errors Preventing Registration".
3. Go to the class overrides and changing audit/credit status page and click Request a class override.
4. Click Apply for New Override and select Registration Error as the override type.
5. Select the class, enter your reason for the override and click Submit Request.
6. Confirm the request appeared on your override dashboard with the status New Request.
7. The request will be processed by the college or department and you will receive an email with the decision.
8. If approved, you must return to the registration channel and register for the class yourself, as registration is not automatic.

title: Cabinet: Can't See All My Files

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. This applies to USask managed Windows devices using Offline Files. Cabinet is marked offline when the device can't reach the network share at logon.
   — If you are off campus, connect to the USask VPN first.
   — On Windows 11, open Control Panel > Windows Tools first.
2. Open your Cabinet folder in File Explorer.
3. Click the Home tab, then Easy Access > Work Online.
4. Refresh the window and confirm all of your Cabinet files are visible.

title: Devices: Basic Hardware Troubleshooting

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
1. Confirm the device powers on and is charged.
2. Reseat cables and try a different port or cable.
3. Restart the device and retest.
4. Record the model and symptoms if the problem persists.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Physical repair of university owned equipment is handled by a technician, not at the desk.

title: Wi-Fi on ChromeOS and Linux: username format

sections.text: On ChromeOS and Linux the wireless identity needs the full username with the domain, not the short username alone. This is the most common first attempt failure.

title: Wi-Fi on a Mac: the administrator password prompt

sections.text: On macOS the certificate trust prompt asks for the Mac's local administrator password. On a personally owned Mac that is the password for the Mac itself, and not knowing it stops the connection.

title: After a password reset: update your saved passwords

sections.text: After a password reset you must update saved wireless networks, VPN, phone mail sync and any password manager. Synchronisation is not instant, so an immediate failure is usually a saved old password rather than a fault.

title: MFA: approving a sign-in instead of typing a code

sections.text: A message asking you to check your registered device is waiting for an approval tap in the authenticator app, not a typed code. With number matching the number on screen is typed into the app.

title: Microsoft 365 works in the browser but not the desktop apps

sections.text: When the browser version works but the desktop apps fail, the cause is usually device registration rather than your licence. The service desk handles this, so open a ticket.

title: Managed software catalogue: university devices only

sections.text: The managed software catalogue only works on university managed Windows devices and needs the VPN when off campus. It is not an option on a personal laptop.
